\textbf{Computational scaling on synthetic evidence} (no held-out data). (a) Number of distinct observation patterns $P$ against the number of edges $N$ for evidence generated from the real observation design (template), from independent annotators and without repeated patterns (stress); dashed vertical line: size of the global universe. (b, c) Wall time and peak memory of the streaming pattern compression. (d) One evaluation of the collapsed log posterior and its gradient. (e) MAP with 10 random restarts (open: extrapolated from the restarts that finished, or projected from evaluation counts, a lower bound). (f) NUTS with 2 chains of 300 warm-up and 300 draws from random starts, a cost benchmark rather than a converged fit; open markers are projections from the steps per iteration of the largest measured run (lowest over the two measurement sessions), which are lower bounds because the steps per iteration grow with $N$, and the vertical bars reach the projection at the tree-depth cap (highest over the sessions), the better estimate at ten times the real size; the same ranges as in Table~\ref{tab:compute-scaling}. Measured times are wall-clock on a shared laptop (Apple M2 Pro, 10 cores, 32 GiB) and are upper bounds of the undisturbed cost.
